mn128:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Park.
mn128:2.1: Now on that occasion the bhikkhus at Kosambī had taken to quarrelling and brawling, and were deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers.
mn128:3.1: Then a certain bhikkhu went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he stood at one side. Standing at one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
mn128:3.2: ‘Venerable sir, here at Kosambī the bhikkhus have taken to quarrelling and brawling, and are deep in disputes, stabbing each other with verbal daggers.
mn128:3.3: Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One went to those bhikkhus out of compassion.’
mn128:3.4: The Blessed One consented in silence.
mn128:4.1: Then the Blessed One went to those bhikkhus and said to them:
mn128:4.2: ‘Enough, bhikkhus, no quarrelling, no brawling, no wrangling, no disputing.’
mn128:4.3: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
mn128:4.4: ‘Let the Blessed One wait, venerable sir.
mn128:4.5: The Blessed One is lord of the Dhamma;
mn128:4.6: let the Blessed One, venerable sir, abide inactive, devoted to a pleasant abiding here and now;
mn128:4.7: it is we who shall be known for this quarrelling, brawling, wrangling, and disputing.’
mn128:4.8: For the second time the Blessed One said to those bhikkhus:
mn128:4.9: ‘Enough, bhikkhus, no quarrelling, no brawling, no wrangling, no disputing.’
mn128:4.10: For the second time that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
mn128:4.11: ‘Let the Blessed One wait, venerable sir.
mn128:4.12: The Blessed One is lord of the Dhamma;
mn128:4.13: let the Blessed One, venerable sir, abide inactive, devoted to a pleasant abiding here and now;
mn128:4.14: it is we who shall be known for this quarrelling, brawling, wrangling, and disputing.’
mn128:4.15: For the third time the Blessed One said to those bhikkhus:
mn128:4.16: ‘Enough, bhikkhus, no quarrelling, no brawling, no wrangling, no disputing.’
mn128:4.17: For the third time that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
mn128:4.18: ‘Let the Blessed One wait, venerable sir.
mn128:4.19: The Blessed One is lord of the Dhamma;
mn128:4.20: let the Blessed One, venerable sir, abide inactive, devoted to a pleasant abiding here and now;
mn128:4.21: it is we who shall be known for this quarrelling, brawling, wrangling, and disputing.’
mn128:5.1: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Kosambī for alms.
mn128:5.2: When he had wandered for alms in Kosambī and had returned from his alms round, after his meal he set his resting place in order, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he uttered these stanzas while standing:
mn128:6.2: there is none thinks himself a fool;
mn128:6.3: the Saṅgha being split, none thinks
mn128:6.4: “I too took part, I helped in this.”
mn128:6.5: They have forgotten wise speech, they talk
mn128:6.6: with minds obsessed by words alone;
mn128:6.7: uncurbed their mouths, they bawl at will;
mn128:6.8: none knows what leads him so to do.
mn128:6.10: he worsted me, he robbed me!”
mn128:6.11: Hate is never allayed in men
mn128:6.14: he worsted me, he robbed me!”
mn128:6.15: Hate is surely allayed in men
mn128:6.18: is never in this world allayed.
mn128:6.22: that here we should restrain ourselves;
mn128:6.23: but those who do recognize this—
mn128:6.27: while bent on pillaging the realm,
mn128:6.28: even these can act in concord;
mn128:6.29: so why can you not do so too?
mn128:6.30: If you can find a trustworthy companion
mn128:6.31: with whom to walk, both virtuous and steadfast,
mn128:6.32: then walk with him content and mindfully,
mn128:6.34: If you can find no trustworthy companion
mn128:6.35: with whom to walk, both virtuous and steadfast,
mn128:6.36: then, as a king who leaves a vanquished kingdom,
mn128:6.37: walk like a tusker in the woods alone.
mn128:6.38: Better it is to walk alone,
mn128:6.39: there is no fellowship with fools.
mn128:6.40: Walk alone, harm none, and know no conflict;
mn128:6.41: be like a tusker in the woods alone.’
mn128:7.1: Then, having uttered these stanzas standing, the Blessed One went to Bālakaloṇakāra village.
mn128:7.2: Now on that occasion the venerable Bhagu was living at Bālakaloṇakāra village.
mn128:7.3: The venerable Bhagu saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.
mn128:7.4: Seeing him, he prepared a seat and water for the feet.
mn128:7.5: The Blessed One sat down on the seat prepared.
mn128:7.6: Having sat down, he washed his feet.
mn128:7.7: The venerable Bhagu paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.
mn128:7.8: When he had done so, the Blessed One said to the venerable Bhagu:
mn128:7.9: ‘I hope that you are keeping well, bhikkhu, that you are comfortable, and that you have no trouble on account of alms-food?’
mn128:7.10: ‘I am keeping well, Blessed One, I am comfortable, and I have no trouble on account of alms-food.’
mn128:7.11: Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged the venerable Bhagu with talk on the Dhamma, after which he got up from his seat and went to the Eastern Bamboo Park.
mn128:8.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimbila were living at the Eastern Bamboo Park.
mn128:8.2: The park-keeper saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.
mn128:8.3: Seeing him, he said to the Blessed One:
mn128:8.4: ‘Do not enter this park, great ascetic.
mn128:8.5: There are three clansmen here seeking their own good.
mn128:9.1: The venerable Anuruddha heard the park-keeper conversing with the Blessed One.
mn128:9.2: Hearing this, he said to the park-keeper:
mn128:9.3: ‘Friend park-keeper, do not keep the Blessed One out.
mn128:9.4: It is our Teacher, the Blessed One, who has arrived.’
mn128:10.1: Then the venerable Anuruddha went to the venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila and said to them:
mn128:10.2: ‘Come out, venerable sirs, come out! Our Teacher, the Blessed One, has arrived.’
mn128:10.3: Then the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Nandiya, and the venerable Kimbila went to meet the Blessed One,
mn128:10.4: and one took his bowl and outer robe, one prepared a seat, and one placed water for washing the feet.
mn128:10.5: The Blessed One sat down on the seat prepared.
mn128:10.6: Having sat down, he washed his feet.
mn128:10.7: Then those venerable ones paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.
mn128:10.8: When they had done so, the Blessed One said to the venerable Anuruddha:
mn128:10.9: ‘I hope that you are all keeping well, Anuruddha, that you are comfortable, and that you have no trouble on account of alms-food?’
mn128:10.10: ‘We are keeping well, Blessed One, we are comfortable, and we have no trouble on account of alms-food.’
mn128:11.1: ‘I hope that you all live in concord and agreement, Anuruddha, as undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes?’
mn128:11.2: ‘Surely we do so, venerable sir, we live in concord and agreement, as undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.’
mn128:11.3: ‘But, Anuruddha, how do you live thus, in concord and agreement, as undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes?’
mn128:12.1: ‘Venerable sir, as to that, I think thus:
mn128:12.2: “It is gain for me, it is great gain for me
mn128:12.3: that I am living with such companions in the holy life.”
mn128:12.4: I maintain bodily acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private,
mn128:12.5: I maintain verbal acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private,
mn128:12.6: I maintain mental acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private.
mn128:12.8: “Why should I not set aside what I am minded to do and do only what these venerable ones are minded to do?”
mn128:12.9: And I set aside what I am minded to do, venerable sir, and I do only what these venerable ones are minded to do.
mn128:12.10: We are different in body, venerable sir, but only one in mind, I think.’
mn128:12.12: and the venerable Kimbila said to the Blessed One:
mn128:12.14: “It is gain for me, it is great gain for me
mn128:12.15: that I am living with such companions in the holy life.”
mn128:12.16: I maintain bodily acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private,
mn128:12.17: I maintain verbal acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private,
mn128:12.18: I maintain mental acts of loving-kindness towards these venerable ones, in public and in private.
mn128:12.20: “Why should I not set aside what I am minded to do and do only what these venerable ones are minded to do?”
mn128:12.21: And I set aside what I am minded to do, venerable sir, and I do only what these venerable ones are minded to do.
mn128:12.22: We are different in body, venerable sir, but only one in mind, I think.
mn128:12.23: That is how we live in concord, venerable sir, as undisputing as milk with water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.’
mn128:13.2: I hope that you all dwell diligent, ardent, and self-controlled?’
mn128:14.2: ‘But, Anuruddha, how do you dwell thus, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled?’
mn128:14.3: ‘Venerable sir, as to that, whichever of us returns first from the village with alms-food prepares the seats, sets out the water for drinking and for washing, and puts the refuse bucket in its place.
mn128:14.4: Whichever of us returns last from the village with alms-food eats any food left over, if he wishes; if he does not wish to, he throws it away where there is no greenery, or he drops it into water where there is no life.
mn128:14.5: He puts away the seats, he puts away the water for drinking and for washing, he puts away the refuse bucket after washing it, and he sweeps out the refectory.
mn128:14.6: Whoever notices that the pot of drinking water or the pot of washing water or the pot for the privy is low or empty sees to it.
mn128:14.7: If it is too heavy for him, he calls someone else by a sign of the hand, and they move it by joining hands; but we do not speak for that purpose, venerable sir.
mn128:14.8: And every five days, venerable sir, we sit out the whole night together in talk on the Dhamma.
mn128:14.9: That is how we dwell diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, venerable sir.’
mn128:15.2: But, Anuruddha, while dwelling thus diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, have you attained as a comfortable abiding any distinction worthy of a Noble One’s knowledge and vision, higher than the human dhamma?’
mn128:15.3: ‘As to that, venerable sir, we, while dwelling diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, perceive both illumination and the vision of forms.
mn128:15.4: But that illumination of ours soon disappears, and so does the vision of forms;
mn128:15.5: and we have not penetrated the sign for that.’
mn128:16.1: ‘Still, Anuruddha, that sign should be penetrated by you.
mn128:16.2: I too, Anuruddha, before my enlightenment, while I was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, perceived both illumination and the vision of forms.
mn128:16.3: But that illumination of mine soon disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:16.5: “What is the reason, what is the condition, why this illumination of mine and the vision of forms disappears?”
mn128:16.7: “Uncertainty arose in me, and owing to uncertainty my concentration died away.
mn128:16.8: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:16.9: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again.”
mn128:17.1: ‘As I dwelt, Anuruddha, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, I perceived illumination and the vision of forms.
mn128:17.2: But that illumination of mine soon disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:17.4: “What is the reason, what is the condition, why this illumination of mine and the vision of forms disappears?”
mn128:17.6: “Inattention arose in me, and owing to inattention my concentration died away.
mn128:17.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:17.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention.”
mn128:18.3: “Lethargy and drowsiness arose in me, and owing to lethargy and drowsiness my concentration died away.
mn128:18.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:18.5: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness.”
mn128:19.3: “Alarm arose in me, and owing to alarm my concentration died away.
mn128:19.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:19.5: Just as, Anuruddha, if a man walking along a road had quails fly up on either side of him, alarm would arise in him on that account;
mn128:19.6: so too, Anuruddha, alarm arose in me, and owing to alarm my concentration died away.
mn128:19.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:19.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm.”
mn128:20.3: “Elation arose in me, and owing to elation my concentration died away.
mn128:20.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:20.5: Just as, Anuruddha, if a man seeking one hidden treasure came upon five hidden treasures all at once, elation would arise in him on that account;
mn128:20.6: so too, Anuruddha, elation arose in me, and owing to elation my concentration died away.
mn128:20.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:20.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation.”
mn128:21.3: “Inertia arose in me, and owing to inertia my concentration died away.
mn128:21.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:21.5: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia.”
mn128:22.3: “Too active an energy arose in me, and owing to too active an energy my concentration died away.
mn128:22.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:22.5: Just as, Anuruddha, if a man gripped a quail tightly with both hands, it would die then and there;
mn128:22.6: so too, Anuruddha, too active an energy arose in me, and owing to too active an energy my concentration died away.
mn128:22.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:22.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia, nor too active an energy.”
mn128:23.3: “Too sluggish an energy arose in me, and owing to too sluggish an energy my concentration died away.
mn128:23.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:23.5: Just as, Anuruddha, if a man gripped a quail loosely, it would fly up out of his hand;
mn128:23.6: so too, Anuruddha, too sluggish an energy arose in me, and owing to too sluggish an energy my concentration died away.
mn128:23.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:23.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia, nor too active an energy, nor too sluggish an energy.”
mn128:24.3: “Longing arose in me, and owing to longing my concentration died away.
mn128:24.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:24.5: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia, nor too active an energy, nor too sluggish an energy, nor longing.”
mn128:25.3: “Perception of diversity arose in me, and owing to perception of diversity my concentration died away.
mn128:25.4: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:25.5: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia, nor too active an energy, nor too sluggish an energy, nor longing, nor perception of diversity.”
mn128:26.1: ‘As I dwelt, Anuruddha, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, I perceived illumination and the vision of forms.
mn128:26.2: But that illumination of mine soon disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:26.4: “What is the reason, what is the condition, why this illumination of mine and the vision of forms disappears?”
mn128:26.6: “Too much meditating upon forms arose in me, and owing to too much meditating upon forms my concentration died away.
mn128:26.7: When concentration died away, the illumination disappeared, and so did the vision of forms.
mn128:26.8: I shall so act that uncertainty does not arise in me again, nor inattention, nor lethargy and drowsiness, nor alarm, nor elation, nor inertia, nor too active an energy, nor too sluggish an energy, nor longing, nor perception of diversity, nor too much meditating upon forms.”
mn128:27.1: ‘Knowing thus, Anuruddha, “Uncertainty is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned uncertainty, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.2: Knowing thus, “Inattention is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned inattention, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.3: Knowing thus, “Lethargy and drowsiness is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned lethargy and drowsiness, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.4: Knowing thus, “Alarm is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned alarm, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.5: Knowing thus, “Elation is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned elation, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.6: Knowing thus, “Inertia is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned inertia, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.7: Knowing thus, “Too active an energy is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned too active an energy, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.8: Knowing thus, “Too sluggish an energy is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned too sluggish an energy, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.9: Knowing thus, “Longing is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned longing, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.10: Knowing thus, “Perception of diversity is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned perception of diversity, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:27.11: Knowing thus, “Too much meditating upon forms is an imperfection of mind,” I abandoned too much meditating upon forms, that imperfection of mind.
mn128:28.1: ‘As I dwelt, Anuruddha, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, I perceived illumination and did not see forms;
mn128:28.2: I saw forms and did not perceive illumination—
mn128:28.3: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day.
mn128:28.5: “What is the reason, what is the condition, why I perceive illumination and do not see forms,
mn128:28.6: and why I see forms and do not perceive illumination,
mn128:28.7: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day?”
mn128:28.9: “On the occasion on which I give attention to the sign of forms without giving attention to the sign of illumination, on that occasion I perceive illumination and do not see forms.
mn128:28.10: But on the occasion on which I give attention to the sign of illumination without giving attention to the sign of forms, on that occasion I see forms and do not perceive illumination—
mn128:28.11: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day.”
mn128:29.1: ‘As I dwelt, Anuruddha, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, I perceived limited illumination and saw limited forms;
mn128:29.2: I perceived measureless illumination and saw measureless forms—
mn128:29.3: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day.
mn128:29.5: “What is the reason, what is the condition, why I perceive limited illumination and see limited forms,
mn128:29.6: and why I perceive measureless illumination and see measureless forms—
mn128:29.7: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day?”
mn128:29.9: “On the occasion on which my concentration is limited, on that occasion my eye is limited.
mn128:29.10: With a limited eye I perceive limited illumination and see limited forms.
mn128:29.11: But on the occasion on which my concentration is measureless, on that occasion my eye is measureless.
mn128:29.12: With a measureless eye I perceive measureless illumination and see measureless forms—
mn128:29.13: for a whole night, for a whole day, for a whole night and day.”
mn128:30.1: ‘As soon as I knew, Anuruddha, “Uncertainty is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.2: As soon as I knew, “Inattention is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.3: As soon as I knew, “Lethargy and drowsiness is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.4: As soon as I knew, “Alarm is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.5: As soon as I knew, “Elation is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.6: As soon as I knew, “Inertia is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.7: As soon as I knew, “Too active an energy is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.8: As soon as I knew, “Too sluggish an energy is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.9: As soon as I knew, “Longing is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.10: As soon as I knew, “Perception of diversity is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:30.11: As soon as I knew, “Too much meditating upon forms is an imperfection of mind,” it was abandoned in me.
mn128:31.2: “The imperfections of my mind have been abandoned by me.
mn128:31.3: Now let me develop concentration in three ways.”
mn128:31.4: So, Anuruddha, I developed concentration with initial application and sustained application; I developed concentration without initial application and with sustained application only; I developed concentration without initial application and without sustained application; I developed concentration accompanied by happiness; I developed concentration without happiness; I developed concentration accompanied by pleasure; I developed concentration accompanied by equanimity.
mn128:32.1: ‘When, Anuruddha, concentration with initial application and sustained application had been developed by me, concentration without initial application and with sustained application only had been developed by me, concentration without initial application and without sustained application had been developed by me, concentration accompanied by happiness had been developed by me, concentration without happiness had been developed by me, concentration accompanied by pleasure had been developed by me, concentration accompanied by equanimity had been developed by me,
mn128:32.2: then knowledge and vision arose in me:
mn128:32.3: “My deliverance is unshakeable; this is the last birth; there is now no more renewal of being.”’
mn128:32.4: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn128:32.5: The venerable Anuruddha was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
